tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Who this connection acts as: user, active org, plan, credit balance, and the scopes granted.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List the org's projects (id, name, kind, status, timestamps), newest first. A connection limited to some projects sees only those.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: One project: status, kind, files, model, published address, preview path.

tools.name: read_project_file
tools.description: Read one text file of a project (relative path such as index.html or app.js).

tools.name: get_publish_check
tools.description: Run the publish gate's checks for a project without publishing (what would block it).

tools.name: list_published_sites
tools.description: Projects that are published, with their public slug and address.

tools.name: list_approvals
tools.description: The org's approval queue (pending by default): publish requests and other actions waiting for a human. Approving happens in the app, not here.

tools.name: get_credits
tools.description: Credit balance and the 50 most recent ledger entries (a connection limited to some projects gets the balance and its own cap only).

tools.name: get_connection
tools.description: This connection: which projects it may use (all, one project, or only the ones it created), its daily credit cap, what it spent today (UTC) and what is left.

tools.name: get_usage_today
tools.description: Today's model usage against the daily cap.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a project from a prompt and build it. tools.description: Same as create_project, for apps that order builds for their customers, but it answers as soon as the build has started (status building, with the projectId): poll get_build_status, then get_result for the delivery link. `idempotencyKey` (e.g. the order id) makes a retry return the same build instea

tools.name: edit_project
tools.description: Apply a follow-up edit prompt to a project (creates a new version; an edit that changes nothing is free). Spends credits (depends on `tier`, default standard). tools.name: confirm_action
tools.description: Run a spending action (create_project, create_build, edit_project) the user confirmed: pass the confirmToken it returned. Each token runs once, within 10 minutes, on this connection only.

tools.name: get_build_status
tools.description: Where a project's build is: queued, building, ready or failed, with its version and preview/public address when ready.

tools.name: get_result
tools.description: The delivery of a finished build: a claim link (single use, 30 days; calling again returns the same open link) that copies the build into the recipient's own Amplify account, plus a preview address at once.

tools.name: publish_project
tools.description: Ask to publish a project at a public address. This goes through the publish gate: it queues an approval that the owner confirms in the app (Approvals tab); nothing goes live until they do.

tools.name: list_custom_domains
tools.description: Custom domains attached to a project and their status (read-only; adding or removing domains is done in the app).

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "create_project" is 676 chars, far longer than this server's median (130). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_project_file · Private data: get_project, read_project_file, create_project, create_build, edit_project, confirm_action · Public sink: get_publish_check, list_approvals, publish_project · Destructive: get_publish_check, create_project, create_build, edit_project, confirm_action.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_project_file · Private data: get_project, read_project_file, create_project, create_build, edit_project, confirm_action · Public sink: get_publish_check, list_approvals, publish_project · Destructive: get_publish_check, create_project, create_build, edit_project, confirm_action

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
